commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The chapter 01 composition defined entry_is_line_a..e as equality tests against five exemplar statistical reporting numbers from other chapters (7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30, 8541.42.00.10), grounding chapter-01 §301 / §122 / reciprocal-exclusion gating on provisions outside this chapter's scope so those branches could never fire for any line chapter 01 actually covers.
triage.triage_notes: Diff is exactly two hunks in every module in this chunk: the module summary (3 lines) plus removal of the 100 lines holding the five derived rules; nothing else changed (no added rules, no formula edits). Downstream consumers still reference the identifiers in this commit (e.g. entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded has formula 'entry_is_line_a', china_301 component sums five 'if entry_is_line_X and origin_is_china' terms), so the identifiers survive as caller inputs under the repo's referenced-implies-input convention; the semantic re-gating lands in the later PR #1300 commits a9562cfd4 'b1.6: generalize generated component surfaces' and 198bee703. Verified through the pinned corpus release that us/statute/hts/7202.11.10.00 is a chapter-72 ferromanganese line ('Containing by weight more than 2 percent but not more than 4 percent of carbon'), i.e. outside chapter 01. The summary sentence 'This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values' is boilerplate carried verbatim from the parent version and describes the sibling-distinctness serialization transform, not this removal; the PR ledger confirms a real surface change ('-500 removed exemplar-flag outputs'). PR body names the defect: 'the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on section 301-member lines for all origins'. Runner-up kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (chapter module carrying another chapter's line semantics); confidence held at 0.7 because the commit message itself is generic and the naming/gating half of the repair is a later commit. Companion .test.yaml files changed in the same commit (100 test files in the bundle).
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute the reading and could not: the diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas are equality tests against statistical reporting numbers belonging to chapters 72, 76, 95, 22 and 85 (`(hts_number == "7202.11.10.00")` … `(hts_number == "8541.42.00.10")`), each carrying its own proof atoms citing those out-of-chapter provisions, from a chapter-01 composition. Those flags were the sole grounding for chapter-01 legal-category rules — `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` (9903.01.32 annex list) had `formula: entry_is_line_a`, `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` (9903.01.33 metals scope) had `formula: entry_is_line_b`, and the §301 China stack and the 9903.05.07 carve-out branch `(if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0 …)` all turn on them — so chapter-01 duty gating was grounded on provisions outside this chapter's scope, and the PR calls that coupling out as having "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins." This is not mechanical: formulas, proof atoms and the module's input/output surface changed (the PR ledger records "−500 removed exemplar-flag outputs"), and it is the removal arm of untraceable_branch (a condition with no basis in the cited source / grounded on the wrong provision), not a boundary, amount, period or polarity error.
triage.verifier_quote: -  source: HTS 7202.11.10.00 statistical reporting number … -  - formula: (hts_number == "7202.11.10.00")
triage.verifier_notes: Caveats a reviewer should weigh. (1) The module's own summary still asserts "This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values … runtime semantics are unchanged" — that is generator boilerplate and is contradicted by the diff, which removes formulas and proof atoms; do not treat it as a denial. (2) Every consuming formula (`entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b`, the §301 slots, §338 gate) is byte-identical before and after; this commit changes only where the flags come from (local derived rule → caller input under the referenced-implies-input convention). If a reviewer scores "meaning change" strictly as a change to surviving formula text, this commit alone looks like an input-surface refactor and the case slides toward unclear. (3) The repair is partial in this file: `entry_is_energy_resource` (cited to 9903.01.13 energy/critical minerals) still reads `- formula: (hts_number == "7202.11.10.00")` at post line 1950, and the other-chapter citation paths remain in `source_verification.corpus_citation_paths`, so the same exemplar-grounding defect survives the commit for at least one rule. (4) The full membership-semantic regating (`entry_is_section_122_exempt` / `entry_is_section_232_covered`) and the new §232 steel component land in sibling commits of PR #1300, so the PR quote in the first reader's justification describes the stacked change, not literally this diff. Verified read-only via `git show` of parent 956a5474 and 2a6bdb01de; no provision lookup was needed because the defect is structural (wrong-chapter grounding), not text-dependent.
